title: Adaptive Quarter Playbook: Hosted Endpoint Line-up & Catalog Commitments
creator: Amina Patel
okrs: Increase hosted API request throughput efficiency by 20%
Reduce median generation cost per 1k tokens by 15%
description:
Purpose: Create a compact, decision-ready quarter playbook that maps plausible demand scenarios to model-catalog commitments, hosted endpoint line-ups, and operational runways. This ticket coordinates cross-functional commitments (product, engineering, design, sales ops) and produces a single artifact (Quarter Scenario Deck + Commit Matrix) used for exec sign-off and runbook handoff to Eng/Ops.

Scope:
- Define 3 demand scenarios (Base / Accelerated / Surge) across latency, cost constraints, and geographic mix.
- For each scenario, propose: model tier lineup (primary/secondary fallbacks), canary windows, capacity buffer commitments (dedicated vs burst), and rollback triggers.
- Map model onboarding backlog items to quarter commit windows and risk grades.
- Produce a Commit Matrix that ties each hosted endpoint to: SLA tier, quantization recommendation, expected token cost delta, and canary % rollout plan.

Deliverables:
- Quarter Scenario Deck (slides) with 1-page runbook per scenario.
- Commit Matrix CSV for operations.
- Stakeholder sign-off log and exec summary.

Acceptance criteria:
- Deck reviewed by Eng + Console + Research with recorded feedback and at least two design mockups for dashboard visuals.
- Commit Matrix validated against staging perf baselines (latency P50/P95) and cost estimates.
- Exec sign-off captured in the attachments.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Conservative line-ups reduce short-term cost but may degrade feature parity for new capabilities.
- Aggressive commits require reserved capacity spend that increases short-term ARR but improves tail-latency guarantees.
- Canary windows may be constrained by regional capacity; fallback policies must be explicit.

Owners & stakeholders: PM (Amina Patel) owner; Eng lead (Diego Ramos) for perf validation; Design (Maya Lin) for dashboard mocks; Sales ops liaison (Elliot Grant) to validate region demand assumptions.

Next steps: finalize scenario inputs with Sales ops (due 2026-03-10), lock perf baselines with Eng (2026-03-18), circulate deck for review (2026-03-22), exec sign-off (target 2026-03-28).
